definitions.explanation: A soft, transparent sea creature that drifts with the current and can sting. Usually written in katakana; the kanji spelling {海月|くらげ} is seen in literary text.

examples.japanese: クラゲ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{刺|さ}された→刺す：02111_sasu⟧。
examples.english: I got stung by a jellyfish.
After Obon, the jellyfish in the sea increase.

examples.japanese: ⟦{水族館|すいぞくかん}→水族館：09220_suizokukan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧クラゲ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{水槽|すいそう}→水槽：09956_suisou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦ライト→ライト：13631_raito⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{照|て}らされて→照らす：04669_terasu⟧⟦とても→とても：00593_totemo⟧⟦きれい→きれい：00717_kirei⟧だった。
examples.english: The jellyfish tank at the aquarium, lit up by the lights, was very beautiful.

notes:
Japanese beaches are said to fill with jellyfish after ⟦お{盆|ぼん}→お盆：05587_obon⟧ in mid-August, which is one reason people stop swimming in the sea then. Salted jellyfish is also eaten, mainly in Chinese-style dishes.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- クラゲ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{刺|さ}される→刺す：02111_sasu⟧: to be stung by a jellyfish
- クラゲ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{漂|ただよ}う→漂う：04356_tadayou⟧: jellyfish drift
- ⟦{海|うみ}→海：00556_umi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧クラゲ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧: jellyfish appear in the sea

WRITING:
- Kana is usual; {海月|くらげ} and {水母|くらげ} are kanji spellings met in literature.
